normalizations.physical_spaces: Real distributions, mean zero. Viewed as 2-periodic; e_k(x)=exp(i*k*pi*x); normalized sesquilinear distribution/test pairing extends (1/2) integral_0^2 f conjugate(g). Odd Fourier coefficients vanish for 1-periodic distributions.
normalizations.weights: <k> = 1 + |k|; norm sup_k <k>^s |q_k|. Birkhoff output weights use n, whereas potential coefficients vanish at odd k; do not silently identify coefficient q_(2n) with q_n.

additional_consequences: The original physical endpoint norm is weak-star lower semicontinuous. Any specified bound is retained under weak-star closure and under limits of eventually bounded nets.

A lower finite-p norm limit of eventually endpoint-bounded original physical potentials is the identical lower distribution of an endpoint potential with the same norm bound and all physical conditions.

For bounded original physical source sets, ambient closure consists exactly of sequential limits within the set; ambient weak-star closedness can be checked with sequences. Maps out of such bounded sets are continuous iff sequentially continuous.
One physical weak-star subsequence converges in every admissible original lower finite-p norm space, with the subsequence chosen before the exponents.
Continuity into bounded physical sets can be tested using all original Fourier coefficients or any admissible lower norm realization.

Arbitrary-filter compact-open weak-star trajectory convergence equals uniform lower norm convergence on every compact time set. On compact domains it has the explicit single-eventual-error-bound-for-all-times criterion.

On bounded physical initial-data sets, sequential uniform lower norm dependence suffices for continuity into the full compact-time weak-star trajectory space. In the article range the lower norm can be the identical original H-minus-one norm.
